questions.q: A project manager is leading the construction project of a luxury residency. Before proceeding with the site excavation process, a government clearance must be issued. What kind of dependency does this describe? *
questions.e: An external dependency is a relationship between project activities and non-project activities. These dependencies usually involve an external organization or entity. In this case, the government clearance is an external factor that must be completed before proceeding with the site excavation process. This is outside the control of the project team and depends on an external entity (the government), making it an external dependency.

questions.q: During the initial planning phase of a complex development project, a project team has identified several stakeholders, including the project sponsor, end-users, regulatory authorities, and the development team. What should the project manager do to ensure that they have a thorough understanding of the various degrees of influence these stakeholders have on project requirements? *

o.t: Conduct one-on-one interviews with each stakeholder to gather their input and preferences.
Send a questionnaire to stakeholders to gather their feedback on project requirements.
Hold a stakeholder workshop to discuss and prioritize project requirements collectively.
Review historical project documents to identify stakeholder influence patterns.

questions.e: Holding a stakeholder workshop allows the project manager to bring all stakeholders together to discuss and prioritize project requirements collectively. This approach ensures that all voices are heard, facilitates understanding of different perspectives, and helps to identify the varying degrees of influence that stakeholders have on the project requirements. It promotes collaboration, helps build consensus, and allows for immediate clarification of any concerns or conflicts.

questions.q: Working in a predictive environment, a project manager has decided to use a three-point estimation with a beta distribution to measure the cost of project activities. Which of the following formulas will they use? *
questions.e: This is the PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) formula used in beta distribution to calculate a weighted average.

questions.q: Adopting a predictive approach to plan an agriculture project, a project manager chooses the ___________ method to estimate the cost by using work breakdown. *
questions.e: In a predictive approach to project management, the bottom-up method is used to estimate costs by breaking down the project work into smaller, more manageable components. This involves detailed estimation of the costs of each work package or activity, and then aggregating these estimates to get the total project cost. This method is considered very accurate but can be time-consuming.

questions.q: A project team is working on determining the dependencies for activities for an ongoing project. What action should the project team take first to manage dependencies successfully? *

o.t: Communicate the dependencies to the sponsor.
Appoint project schedulers for all tasks.

questions.e: The first action the project team should take to manage dependencies successfully is to assess and document them. This involves identifying and understanding the relationships and interdependencies between activities. By documenting these dependencies, the project team can plan and schedule the project activities more effectively, ensuring that all dependencies are managed and monitored throughout the project lifecycle. Once dependencies are documented, they can be communicated to stakeholders, monitored, and tracked accordingly.

questions.q: You have just been promoted to a project manager position. You are assigned to manage your first project. You want to report your project schedule. You asked a more experienced project manager about the best method to report your schedule. He told you there are several methods to report your schedule like network diagrams, milestone chart and Gantt chart. Under which circumstances is it best to use a network diagram rather than Gantt chart? *

o.t: Gantt chart is always the best way to report project schedule.
To track progress or to report to the team.

questions.e: A network diagram is particularly useful for illustrating the interdependencies between activities in a project. It shows the sequence of tasks and how they are connected, which is crucial for understanding the relationships and dependencies among tasks. While a Gantt chart is excellent for tracking progress and providing a visual timeline, a network diagram is better suited for demonstrating how activities are linked and for analyzing the critical path of a project.

questions.q: A project has begun to develop a new software application that will be used by the company's sales team. The project is expected to take six months to complete and has a budget of $100,000. The project manager has identified software development tools, hardware, and training to be procured. What is the most important thing for the project manager to do while developing the procurement plan? *

o.t: Ensure that all resources will be procured within budget.
Ensure that the project is on schedule with no delays.
Ensure that all procured resources are of great quality.
Ensure that all resources will be procured on schedule.

questions.e: Cost should not exceed allotted budget.

questions.q: Susan is a project manager for a new software project. This type of projects has not been previously done before by her company and she has never managed a similar project to this one. What is the best method of estimating the time for activities that have not previously been done by her company? *
questions.e: When managing a project with activities that have not been previously done by the company and without prior experience in similar projects, three-point estimating is a robust method. It involves estimating the time required for an activity based on three scenarios: the most optimistic (best case), the most pessimistic (worst case), and the most likely (expected case). This method helps in reducing bias, uncertainty, and risks in the estimates by considering a range of outcomes. While other methods like analogous or parametric estimating can be useful in other contexts, three-point estimating is particularly effective in new or uncertain projects.

questions.q: Product scope management involves the requirements that relate to the product of the project. Project scope management involves: *

o.t: The work the project manager will do to manage the project.
The project management efforts done by the project manager.
All work included in the scope management plan.
The work the project will do to deliver the product scope.

questions.e: Project scope management focuses on defining and controlling what work is included in the project. It ensures that the project includes all the work required, and only the work required, to complete the project successfully. This involves planning, defining, validating, and controlling the project scope to deliver the product scope, which is the requirements related to the product of the project.

questions.q: Barbara is managing a large industrial project. Recently, her company received many complaints due to defects found by the customer in the first deliverable. The customer is not satisfied at all with the first project deliverable. The project sponsor is very angry and told her that the company may lose the contract with the customer if they find defects in the next deliverables. In order to reduce sponsor's stress, she told him that they will compare the product's quality standards to those of other comparable successful products to identify best practices and increase the probability of customer acceptance. Which tool is she using? *
questions.e: Benchmarking is the process of comparing the current project's quality standards and performance with those of other successful projects or products to identify best practices and improve the quality and acceptance of the deliverables. By using benchmarking, Barbara aims to identify and adopt quality standards and practices that have been proven successful in similar projects, thereby increasing the likelihood of meeting customer expectations and retaining the contract.

questions.q: During the initiation phase of a project, the project manager wants to gather requirements from a diverse group of stakeholders. Which technique is most effective for capturing a broad range of perspectives in a short period? *
questions.e: Brainstorming allows stakeholders to generate ideas quickly, providing a broad range of potential requirements for further refinement. Focus Groups (A) involve more structured discussions, not rapid idea generation. Delphi Technique (C) is used for expert consensus over multiple rounds. Nominal Group Technique (D) involves ranking and prioritization rather than open idea collection.

questions.q: A project manager needs to collect requirements from a dispersed group of experts while avoiding the influence of dominant participants. Which technique is most suitable? *
questions.e: Delphi Technique gathers expert opinions anonymously, reducing bias and ensuring balanced input from all participants. Focus Groups (B) involve interactive discussions but are subject to dominant personalities. Requirements Workshops (C) allow collaboration but do not eliminate bias. Benchmarking (D) compares against industry best practices but does not collect original requirements.

questions.q: Which requirement collection technique uses visual representations to clarify relationships between different system components? *
questions.e: Context diagrams visually depict system interactions, helping stakeholders understand data flows and dependencies. Document Analysis (B) reviews records but does not create visual representations. Delphi Technique (C) collects expert feedback but does not create diagrams. Brainstorming (D) generates ideas but does not map system relationships.

questions.q: A company is launching a new software product and wants to collect structured feedback from a large number of customers. Which technique is most appropriate? *
questions.e: Surveys and questionnaires allow structured data collection from a large audience efficiently. Interviews (A) are time-consuming and unsuitable for large groups. Brainstorming (C) is an idea-generation tool rather than a structured feedback mechanism. Document Analysis (D) reviews existing documents rather than gathering new input.

questions.q: A project manager facilitates a meeting where each stakeholder ranks their most important requirements by assigning numerical values. What technique is being used? *
questions.e: Nominal Group Technique involves ranking and prioritizing requirements collectively to ensure balanced decision-making. Delphi Technique (B) is used for expert consensus rather than numerical ranking. Brainstorming (C) generates ideas but does not prioritize them numerically. Context Diagrams (D) are used for system visualization rather than ranking.

questions.q: A project manager consults a panel of industry experts to estimate costs based on their experience and insights. What estimating technique is being used? *
questions.e: Expert judgment relies on industry specialists to provide informed estimates based on their experience. Delphi Technique (A) gathers expert opinions anonymously rather than direct consultation. Analogous Estimating (C) compares historical projects rather than relying on expert opinions. Monte Carlo Simulation (D) uses statistical modeling rather than expert experience.

questions.q: A company follows the rule that project costs should be estimated by doubling the best-case scenario costs to account for potential risks. Which technique is being used? *
questions.e: Heuristic estimating applies predefined rules or "rules of thumb," such as doubling estimates to account for risks. Analogous estimating (B) uses past projects rather than heuristics. Three-Point Estimating (C) calculates weighted averages rather than applying fixed multipliers. Bottom-up estimating (D) builds estimates from individual tasks rather than using general rules.

questions.q: A project team needs to make a decision on the best approach for executing a critical task. The project manager asks all members to vote, and the option with the highest number of votes is selected. What type of voting technique is being used? *
questions.e: Majority voting requires more than 50% of the votes for an option to be selected. Unanimity (B) requires all members to agree. Plurality (C) selects the option with the most votes, even if it does not exceed 50%. Delphi Technique (D) involves expert consensus over multiple rounds rather than open voting.

questions.q: A project manager is developing a project management plan, but several key stakeholders have conflicting expectations regarding project scope. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Proceed with the project plan based on the sponsor’s expectations.
Hold a stakeholder meeting to align expectations and clarify scope.
Document all stakeholder expectations separately and address them later.
Use expert judgment to finalize the scope based on best practices.

questions.e: Stakeholder alignment is crucial before finalizing the project scope. Ignoring stakeholder concerns (A, C) could lead to resistance or scope creep. Using expert judgment alone (D) does not resolve conflicts among stakeholders.

questions.q: During schedule planning, a critical supplier informs the project manager of a potential delay in material delivery. What is the best approach? *

o.t: Accept the delay and adjust the project schedule accordingly.
Identify alternative suppliers and include a contingency plan.
Expedite the other project activities to compensate for the delay.
Escalate the issue to senior management for resolution.

questions.e: Risk management is essential in planning—identifying alternatives prevents delays. Simply accepting delays (A) without action affects project completion. Expediting other activities (C) may not mitigate the specific risk. Escalation (D) is premature without first seeking a solution.

questions.q: A project manager is developing the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) but realizes that some work packages are too high-level. What should be done? *

o.t: Decompose the work packages further into more manageable tasks.
Assign the existing work packages to team leads for interpretation.
Proceed with the current WBS and refine it during execution.
Use a rolling wave planning approach for future clarification.

questions.e: A properly structured WBS breaks work into smaller, manageable components. Leaving high-level work packages (B, C) creates ambiguity and poor project tracking. Rolling wave planning (D) is used when detailed planning is not possible, but here, decomposition is the correct approach.

questions.q: While estimating project costs, a senior executive asks the project manager to reduce the budget without impacting scope. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Apply value engineering techniques to optimize project costs.
Reduce the scope to match the new budget constraints.
Increase resource efficiency without changing project activities.
Request a formal change request for budget reduction.

questions.e: Value engineering identifies cost-effective ways to achieve project objectives without reducing scope. Reducing scope (B) affects deliverables and requires stakeholder approval. Increasing efficiency (C) is helpful but may not meet budget constraints. A formal change request (D) is needed only if major budget adjustments are required.

questions.q: During the planning phase, the project sponsor requests that the project be completed two months earlier than originally scheduled. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Evaluate schedule compression techniques such as crashing or fast-tracking.
Update the project schedule immediately to reflect the new deadline.
Inform the sponsor that the deadline cannot be changed without reducing scope.
Adjust resource allocations to accelerate work through on-boarding resources from another nearly-finished complementary project.

questions.e: Before making any changes, the project manager must analyze schedule compression options (crashing adds resources, fast-tracking overlaps tasks). Updating the schedule immediately (B) without analysis may lead to unrealistic planning. Rejecting the request outright (C) without exploring options may cause stakeholder dissatisfaction. Adjusting resources (D) without analysis could create inefficiencies.

questions.q: A project manager is defining resource requirements but is unsure about future workload distribution. What should be done? *

o.t: Use a resource histogram to visualize resource allocation over time.
Assign generic roles and define details later.
Estimate resources based on team experience and expert judgment.
Finalize resource allocation based on current project phase only.

questions.e: A resource histogram helps visualize workload distribution and balance resources effectively. Assigning generic roles (B) may lead to inefficiencies. Expert judgment (C) is useful but lacks quantitative analysis. Focusing only on the current phase (D) ignores future resource demands.

questions.q: A project sponsor wants to ensure full alignment before finalizing a key decision. The project team discusses all options thoroughly until every member agrees on the final choice. What type of voting technique is this? *
questions.e: Unanimity means all participants must agree on the decision before proceeding. Plurality (B) selects the option with the most votes, even if not all agree. Majority voting (C) only requires more than 50% agreement. Delphi Technique (D) is an anonymous expert consensus method, not open discussion.
